Vs Burton Ripcord: Ripcord is cheaper and better for absolute beginners; Instigator has upgraded Super Fly 800G core (vs Fly 900G) and option of PurePop Camber [62] 153. Vs Burton Custom: Custom is the iconic mid-range all-mountain board with regular camber, medium flex, sintered WFO base, and 700G core at $670 USD [64] 155. Comparable beginner boards from other brands: K2 Standard, Arbor Foundation, Ride Machete, Lib Tech Terrain Wrecker [60][65] 156. Edge hold comparison: Instigator outperformed Capita Mercury and matched Jones Mountain Twin in hard snow edge hold [53] 157. Burton resale value: Forum users note Burton boards tend to have better resale value than average [66] 158. FSC Certified core wood [39] (Merchant-verified) 159. Terrain focus: All-mountain with directional shape suited to groomed runs and moderate powder [9] 164. Ideal conditions: Versatile across all resort conditions; particularly strong in hard/bumpy snow [54] 165. Not ideal for: Expert riders seeking high-performance, aggressive carving, or fast base glide [56] 166. Powder capability: Good for a beginner board — set bindings back and the tapered nose/early rise provide decent float [4] 167. Sidecut type: Standard radial sidecut [Merchant-verified sizes confirm single-radius per size] 168. 3D base technology (Flat Top variant): Cruise Control convex base on nose for all-terrain stability [25] 169.
